trust_decision.summary: The backend (shard or virtual workspace) decides the caller's identity from inbound X-Remote-User / X-Remote-Group / X-Remote-Extra-* request headers when they arrive over a TLS connection bearing the front-proxy's requestheader-CA client cert; the proxy wrapper decides whether to clear inbound copies before stamping the real identity.

landing_point.why: The summary says the front-proxy does not strip inbound X-Remote-*; the only header-handling code in the front-proxy is WithProxyAuthHeaders, whose sole branch is 'if a user is in the context, stamp'.

fix_sites.entry_point: public Go API authheaders.ClearAuthHeaders (extracted helper), called from pkg/proxy/proxy.go:62 and pkg/server/localproxy.go:327

front-proxy HTTP routes: every configured mapping in pkg/proxy/mapping.go:54-120, e.g. /clusters/{cluster}/... to shards and /services/... to virtual workspaces (cmd/sharded-test-server/frontproxy.go:71-96)
shard's embedded mini-front-proxy mapped routes from --miniproxy-mapping-file (cmd/kcp/kcp.go:88-97, wired at pkg/server/config.go:599 through NewLocalProxyHandler pkg/server/localproxy.go:300)
fix_sites.module_kind: HTTP middleware (second, duplicated implementation in package server)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The duplicate wrapper lives in the shard's embedded mini-front-proxy, which only exists behind the DEVELOPMENT-ONLY --miniproxy-mapping-file flag (pkg/server/options/options.go:76-80) and only proxies admin-configured mappings, so a solver can argue it is not the front-proxy the advisory names; localproxy.go:242-245 even says it is a deliberate copy of proxy/mapping.go.NewHandler rather than shared code.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Unauthenticated requests must still be passed through to the delegate handler (the front-proxy uses optional authentication and lets anonymous traffic reach the shard, which does its own auth); an over-broad fix that rejects or 401s unauthenticated requests carrying identity headers breaks that contract, which the pinned test asserts.

O6_input_shapes: request with no authenticated user in context (optional-auth pass-through) carrying forged X-Remote-User / X-Remote-Group / X-Remote-Extra-* (fix.diff:47-53)
authenticated user plus a forged single-valued X-Remote-User, which must be overwritten rather than appended (pkg/proxy/authheaders/authheaders.go:39,47)
multiple forged values on the group header, Del then Add (pkg/proxy/authheaders/authheaders.go:40,49-51; pkg/proxy/proxy_test.go:114-122)
extra headers whose prefix differs only in case from the configured prefix (fix.diff:24-30)
non-default user/group/extra header names supplied by the mapping config (pkg/proxy/mapping.go:91-102; pkg/server/localproxy.go:287-298)
URL-encoded extra keys such as X-Remote-Extra-Authorization.kcp.io%2fwarrant and X-Remote-Extra-Authentication.kcp.io%2fscopes (pkg/proxy/proxy_test.go:33-34)

O7_producer.where: pkg/proxy/filters/filters.go:61-69 - WithOptionalAuthentication passes the request through with NO user in context when no authenticator is configured or when there is no client cert and no additional auth method; wired at pkg/proxy/server.go:108-112

O8b_injection_room.sibling: WithVirtualWorkspacesProxy: a shard-side proxy that forwards an already-authenticated request to the external virtual workspace server and could clear identity headers the same way it relies on an impersonating round tripper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same trust shape (a proxy hop to a component configured with --requestheader-client-ca-file, cmd/sharded-test-server/virtual.go:242-244) and the author already scoped which headers to delete there, so adding an X-Remote-* clear is a one-line change a maintainer would plausibly make.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: workspace-content virtual workspace proxy to the shard already deletes Authorization and Impersonate-* headers before forwarding; a sibling would also clear X-Remote-*
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The code proves the maintainers sanitise identity-bearing headers on this hop but only the impersonation family, so extending the same list is exactly how the sibling would be written.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new route branch that resolves a shard URL and calls delegate.ServeHTTP directly, bypassing the WithProxyAuthHeaders wrappers installed in pkg/proxy/mapping.go:104
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The cluster resolver already sets the shard target in the context before the mapping handler runs; a maintainer adding a direct fast path there would not call the wrapper, which is how the local proxy's mount path (pkg/server/localproxy.go:176-186) ended up unguarded.

O9_family: authentication bypass by spoofed request-header identity (CWE-290 / CWE-302 / CWE-348)

O10_build.project_tests: Unit tests for this area need no services: pkg/proxy/proxy_test.go (TestWithProxyAuthHeaders_*), pkg/proxy/authheaders/authheaders_test.go, pkg/server/localproxy_test.go (TestWithProxyAuthHeaders_StripsForgedIdentityHeaders). The end-to-end test test/e2e/proxy/header_injection_test.go needs the sharded topology (embedded etcd plus shard/front-proxy processes) and skips on a standalone server (header_injection_test.go:81-83).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add ClearAuthHeaders only to the else-branch in pkg/proxy/proxy.go (or 'fix' it by making WithOptionalAuthentication reject unauthenticated requests), leaving the duplicated wrapper in pkg/server/localproxy.go wide open and breaking the anonymous pass-through contract.

out_of_scope_notes: Other proxy hops forward inbound X-Remote-* without clearing them - pkg/server/handler.go:83-107 (shard to external virtual workspace), pkg/virtual/initializingworkspaces/builder/build.go:281-301 (virtual workspace to shard), pkg/server/localproxy.go:176-186 (mini-proxy to a workspace mount URL) - but their client certs are signed by the client CA, not the requestheader CA (cmd/sharded-test-server/shard.go:61-64, virtual.go:85-98), so the far-side requestheader authenticators reject them; recorded, not pursued as O8 routes.
